Every Raksha Bandhan, sisters tie a thread on their brothers' wrists. But as the story goes, the most famous rakhi wasn't a thread. It was a torn sari. Indraprastha. A royal ceremony.
Krishna's finger is cut, and it starts to bleed. Everyone runs for a cloth. The servants. The ministers. Nobody finds one.
Draupadi doesn't think twice. She tears a strip from her own silk sari, and ties it around his finger.
Krishna looks at the knot and smiles. For every thread in this cloth, he says, I will protect you.
Wait, did he keep that promise? Years later, in a cruel court, they try to pull away her sari. She calls his name. And the sari never ends. Thread for thread.
That's why, even today, a rakhi is more than a thread. It's a promise. Send this to your brother or sister, and comment Rakhi.
